text: Source: supplied synopsis and front-page DOCX. The guide spelling and whether there are one or two guides conflict across the supplied documents, so this remains a placeholder. Two team-member details are missing.
One interface, two distinct legal NLP tasks
The outputs support document review; they do not make legal determinations.

Indian Supreme Court judgments → concise draft summaries.

Training and evaluation: IN-Abs judgment–headnote pairs.

Commercial contract passages → eight possible clause categories.

Training and evaluation: CUAD, a non-Indian corpus.
The two tasks have separate data, models and metrics. No combined “legal accuracy” is claimed.
The synopsis proposes summarization and clause classification. Actual contract benchmarking uses CUAD from SEC/EDGAR filings, so performance on Indian contracts is unknown. See docs/DATA_CARD.md.
Acquire public corpora; verify spans and metadata; split by document; prevent duplicate leakage.
Benchmark TF-IDF models against fine-tuned LEGAL-BERT and T5-small on the same held-out subsets.
Accept searchable PDF, DOCX or TXT; show summaries or clause labels; export the output.
Objectives follow the executed pilot, not the unexecuted full-dataset aspiration. Sources: docs/DATA_CARD.md, docs/EXPERIMENT_RESULTS.md, docs/DEMO_AND_VIVA.md.
Domain-specific legal language models help, but results depend on corpus and evaluation setting.
Use contextual representations for specialist vocabulary and long-form legal structure.
Indian case summaries demand outcome coverage, not only lexical overlap.
A reproducible, local comparison across both tasks, with visible baselines, data provenance and failure analysis.
Selected literature and dataset citations are on the final slide; full 20-item journal survey is in the report.

This is not a novelty or priority claim. Literature survey and indexed bibliography: research/LITERATURE_REVIEW.md and reports/Final_Report.pdf. Operational dataset papers: Shukla et al. AACL 2022 for IN-Abs; The Atticus Project for CUAD.
Published corpus sizes and executed pilot sizes are stated separately.
CUAD is not an Indian contract benchmark.

IN-Abs: published 7,130 pairs, two empty train pairs; retained pool after grouping 5,949/1,050/100; executed pilot 64/12/20. CUAD v1: 510 published, official 408/102 split; retained 345/61/102; executed pilot 40/10/10. See docs/DATA_CARD.md and dataset URLs in final references.
Verified answer spans are projected onto bounded passages; this is weak labeling.
Reconstruct 510 contracts and check every answer offset against untouched text.
Group near duplicates, reserve official test, then create ≤256-token passages.
Mark any passage overlapping an answer span; allow multiple of eight labels.
Eight labels: Governing Law · Non-Compete · Exclusivity · Anti-Assignment · Termination for Convenience · Cap on Liability · Audit Rights · Post-Termination Services

Zero invalid CUAD answer offsets were found. Any-character overlap yields an 8-dimensional binary label, so a positive may include a partial clause; zero means no selected annotation, not legal safety. Training negatives capped at 3 per positive; evaluation retains all. Source: docs/DATA_CARD.md.
Long judgment handling is an explicit trade-off
A complete judgment is read for selection, but only selected text enters T5-small.
Extract searchable text from PDF, DOCX or TXT; preserve names, citations and negation.
TF-IDF relevance + redundancy control; restore source order under a token budget.
Compare an extractive baseline with one-epoch fine-tuned T5-small.
Pilot cap: 512 selected input tokens → 128 output tokens. Mean selected training-source coverage: 16%.

All 64 training and all 12 validation target headnotes exceeded the 128-token cap and were shortened; held-out references stayed full length. T5 cannot claim full-document comprehension. Source: docs/DATA_CARD.md.
Baselines remain essential because the fine-tuned models are trained on small pilot samples.

LEGAL-BERT + eight sigmoid outputs
3 epochs · 1,636 train passages
Runs were CPU-only. Model weights, predictions and metrics are stored locally.
LEGAL-BERT trained 3 epochs (723.75 s), T5-small 1 epoch (152.02 s), CPU 4 threads. Checkpoints and metrics in artifacts/pilot. No full-corpus run is claimed.
Document-level partitions precede passage creation; test data are not used to choose thresholds.
10 held-out CUAD contracts → 2,404 passages. Report macro / weighted F1 and exact multi-label subset accuracy.
20 held-out Indian judgments. Report ROUGE-1 / ROUGE-2 / ROUGE-L versus full reference headnotes.
2,340 of 2,404 classifier test passages have none of the eight selected labels; accuracy alone is misleading.

Document duplicate groups are separated before splitting; exact repeated cross-split passage strings are quarantined. Approximate duplicate matching is not exhaustive. Threshold chosen on validation macro F1. See docs/DATA_CARD.md and docs/EXPERIMENT_RESULTS.md.
Same 2,404 held-out passages from 10 non-Indian CUAD contracts; scores 0–1.
Subset accuracy: 0.970 → 0.972; always-zero prediction would score 0.973 because negatives dominate.
Rare classes remain weak; Exclusivity has only 3 positive test passages.

Exact metrics: TF-IDF macro F1 0.385256, weighted 0.408894, accuracy 0.970050; LEGAL-BERT macro 0.447039, weighted 0.509143, accuracy 0.972130. Test rows 2404, all-zero 2340. Source: artifacts/pilot/tfidf/test/metrics.json and artifacts/pilot/legalbert/test/metrics.json (also docs/EXPERIMENT_RESULTS.md).
Held-out IN-Abs test: 20 Indian judgment–headnote pairs; ROUGE scores 0–1.
Only 64 training pairs and 1 epoch. The 512-token selected input covered roughly 16% of training source text on average.
Lexical overlap is not a legal-faithfulness test; disposition must be checked against the source.

Exact scores: extractive R1 0.2164466, R2 0.1200588, RL 0.1445487. T5 R1 0.1494678, R2 0.0797391, RL 0.1045632. All held-out references full length. Source: artifacts/pilot/extractive/test/metrics.json and artifacts/pilot/t5/test/metrics.json.
Failure analysis: what the scores conceal
Interpretation should follow error cases, not only aggregate averages.
Three categories have small positive support. The transformer misses some instances and creates false positives.
Source selection can omit the final order. Fluent short text can miss the legal disposition or a key qualification.
The app exposes source text, selected units and outputs so users can verify them.

Classification: Exclusivity has 3 positives; Post-Termination Services 8. A reviewed test judgment (~3,542 words) showed disposition omission in a generated summary. These examples motivate source-side checks. See docs/EXPERIMENT_RESULTS.md and reports/Final_Report.pdf.
The sample texts demonstrate the interface, not benchmark performance.
Paste a synthetic judgment; compare extractive and T5 outputs; inspect retained source coverage.
Paste a synthetic contract; compare TF-IDF and LEGAL-BERT labels and scores.
Save TXT / JSON summary or CSV / JSON clauses; open the report and saved metric JSONs.
Input: searchable PDF, DOCX, TXT. Scanned PDFs need OCR outside this app.

Run scripts/run_demo.ps1 and open localhost:8501. Existing local checkpoints are available in this workspace. Synthetic demo inputs are examples/demo_judgment.txt and examples/demo_contract.txt. The copied ZIP needs setup and retraining. See docs/DEMO_AND_VIVA.md.
What this pilot establishes — and what comes next
A transparent baseline-to-transformer comparison is possible on a modest local machine.

• Reproducible preprocessing and held-out splits
• Genuine LEGAL-BERT and T5 fine-tuning
• Working local demo and export
• Baselines expose mixed outcomes

• Full-corpus experiments
• Independent Indian contract annotations
• Longer-input summarization and OCR
• Expert review of summary faithfulness
Use the system as review assistance, with the source document beside every output.

Do not characterize the pilot as validated for Indian contract review. Full-corpus configuration exists but has not been executed. Other work includes multilingual evaluation and calibrated probabilities. Source: docs/DATA_CARD.md and docs/DEMO_AND_VIVA.md.
